title: Long idle, short active
hook: A small load lasts many hours. Does duration make it larger than the active load?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities

misconception: The state lasting the most hours must consume the most energy.

claims.text: Illustrative daily loads: active 60W for 2h, idle 3W for 22h. Constant power is assumed. Scaled model; illustrative:60W×2h/day;3W×22h/day;€0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Days=5, A=0.6kWh and B=0.33kWh. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",60,2,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",3,22,"x"],1000]; x denotes Days. At x=5, A=0.6, B=0.33; recall at x=8: B=0.528. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Multiply each power by its own duration before comparing. The longer idle period contributes energy, yet under these stated numbers it remains below active use. No actual appliance rating is implied.

claims.text: Illustrative daily loads: active 60W for 2h, idle 3W for 22h. Constant power is assumed. Change only Days to 8. What is B (Idle) now? Correct: 0.528kWh. Use B's stated rule with Days=8: it gives 0.528kWh. Multiply each power by its own duration before comparing. The longer idle period contributes energy, yet under these stated numbers it remains below active use. No actual appliance rating is implied.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff.

safety.assumptions: Illustrative daily loads: active 60W for 2h, idle 3W for 22h. Constant power is assumed.
